---
title: "03 - Embedding Analysis"
subtitle: "Survival and pathway associations in site-corrected embeddings"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Tests whether Prov-GigaPath embeddings carry prognostic and molecular signal
after within-cancer site correction (02). Raw embeddings are analysed
alongside corrected ones, so the effect of correction is visible.

Inputs: `embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds`, `embed_raw_by_cancer.rds`,
`meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds`, `omics_by_cancer.rds`

Outputs: `surv_all.rds`, `gsva_scores_by_cancer.rds`, `clin_vars_by_cancer.rds`
(all used in 05), `pathway_results.rds`, `cindex_summary.rds`,
`oof_risk_scores.rds`, `Table3_1_full.xlsx`

| Output |
|---|---|
| Figure 3.1 | Did site correction change which dimensions predict survival? |
| Table 3.1 | Which prognostic dimensions track which Hallmark pathways? |
| Table 3.2 | Does the slide alone predict survival at unseen sites, and how close to clinical variables? |
| Table 3.3 | Does the slide add prognostic information beyond age, stage and grade? |
| Figure 3.2 | What biology characterises patients the slide model calls high-risk? |
| Tables S3.1 to S3.4, Figure S3.1 | Dimension counts, site signal, replication across cancers, random vs site-held-out folds |

## Libraries

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
#| output: false
library(tidyr)       # pivot_longer / pivot_wider
library(tibble)      # rownames_to_column
library(survival)    # Surv, coxph, concordance
library(glmnet)      # elastic-net Cox (4.1 or later, for Surv responses)
library(GSVA)        # ssGSEA pathway scores
library(msigdbr)     # Hallmark gene sets
library(ggplot2)     # figures
library(gt)          # tables
library(writexl)     # Excel export of the full Table 3.1
library(dplyr)       # loaded last so its verbs are not masked
```

## Load data

```{r load}
data_dir <- "data"

embed_corrected_by_cancer <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
embed_raw_by_cancer       <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embed_raw_by_cancer.rds"))
meta_corrected_by_cancer  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
omics_by_cancer           <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "omics_by_cancer.rds"))

# Only cancers that were corrected in 02
main_cancers <- intersect(c("KIRC", "COAD", "LUAD", "OV", "READ"), names(embed_corrected_by_cancer))
cat("Analysing:", paste(main_cancers, collapse = ", "), "\n")

embed_corrected <- embed_corrected_by_cancer[main_cancers]   # ComBat, patients x 768
embed_raw       <- embed_raw_by_cancer[main_cancers]         # uncorrected, for comparison
meta            <- meta_corrected_by_cancer[main_cancers]    # survival, TSS, clinical
omics           <- omics_by_cancer[main_cancers]             # RNA-seq for GSVA

fdr_thresh <- 0.05
set.seed(42)
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- General ----

# Experiments are named like "KIRC_RNASeq2GeneNorm-20160128": match by pattern
get_assay <- function(omics_list, pattern) {
  if (is.null(omics_list)) return(NULL)
  idx <- grep(pattern, names(omics_list), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NULL)
  omics_list[[idx[1]]]
}

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "-", ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, d = 3) {                     # "0.650 (0.600 to 0.700)"
  f <- paste0("%.", d, "f (%.", d, "f to %.", d, "f)")
  ifelse(is.na(est), NA_character_, sprintf(f, est, lo, hi))
}

# "HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB" -> "TNFA Signaling Via NFKB" (same function used in 05)
clean_pw <- function(x) {
  caps <- c("DNA", "UV", "MYC", "E2F", "G2M", "TNFA", "NFKB", "IL2", "STAT5", "IL6",
            "JAK", "STAT3", "KRAS", "MTORC1", "PI3K", "AKT", "MTOR", "TGF", "WNT",
            "P53", "UP", "DN", "V1", "V2")
  words <- strsplit(gsub("_", " ", sub("^HALLMARK_", "", x)), " ")
  vapply(words, function(w)
    paste(ifelse(w %in% caps, w, paste0(substr(w, 1, 1), tolower(substring(w, 2)))),
          collapse = " "), character(1))
}

# Two-sided P for a Spearman correlation (t approximation, the same as
# cor.test(exact = FALSE) and as used in 05, so all pathway P-values match)
spearman_p <- function(r, n) {
  t <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / pmax(1 - r^2, 1e-12))
  2 * pt(-abs(t), df = n - 2)
}

# Adjusted R2 of site for every embedding column at once (from group means)
site_adj_r2 <- function(E, g) {
  g   <- droplevels(as.factor(g))
  n_g <- as.vector(table(g))                                 # patients per site
  mu  <- colMeans(E)                                         # overall mean per dimension
  M   <- rowsum(E, g) / n_g                                  # site means
  ssb <- colSums(n_g * sweep(M, 2, mu)^2)                    # between-site sum of squares
  sst <- colSums(sweep(E, 2, mu)^2)                          # total sum of squares
  r2  <- ssb / sst
  n <- nrow(E); k <- nlevels(g)
  1 - (1 - r2) * (n - 1) / (n - k)                           # adjust for number of sites
}

# ---- Univariable Cox per embedding dimension ----
# fdr_thresh = 1 returns every dimension that could be fitted
get_survival_coefficients <- function(embed_mat, meta_df, time_col = "time",
                                      event_col = "event", fdr_thresh = 0.05,
                                      standardize = TRUE) {

  common <- intersect(rownames(embed_mat), rownames(meta_df))    # align patients
  embed  <- embed_mat[common, , drop = FALSE]
  meta   <- meta_df[common, , drop = FALSE]

  time  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta[[time_col]]))
  event <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta[[event_col]]))
  valid <- complete.cases(time, event) & time > 0                # usable survival
  embed <- embed[valid, , drop = FALSE]
  time  <- time[valid]
  event <- event[valid]

  if (nrow(embed) < 10 || sum(event == 1) < 5) {                 # Cox not estimable
    warning("Too few patients or events; skipping.")
    return(NULL)
  }

  surv_obj <- Surv(time, event)
  n <- ncol(embed)
  logHR <- CI_low <- CI_high <- pval <- rep(NA_real_, n)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    x <- embed[, i]
    if (standardize) {                                           # HR per 1 SD
      s <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (is.na(s) || s == 0) next                               # constant dimension
      x <- as.numeric(scale(x))
    }
    fit <- tryCatch(coxph(surv_obj ~ x), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit)) next                                       # one bad fit does not stop the loop

    logHR[i] <- coef(fit)[1]
    ci <- suppressWarnings(try(exp(confint(fit)), silent = TRUE))
    if (!inherits(ci, "try-error")) { CI_low[i] <- ci[1, 1]; CI_high[i] <- ci[1, 2] }
    pval[i] <- summary(fit)$coefficients[1, 5]
  }

  ok  <- !is.na(pval)
  fdr <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  fdr[ok] <- p.adjust(pval[ok], method = "BH")                   # BH across dimensions

  res <- data.frame(Feature = colnames(embed), LogHR = logHR, HR = exp(logHR),
                    CI_low = CI_low, CI_high = CI_high, P_value = pval, FDR = fdr,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  res[!is.na(res$FDR) & res$FDR <= fdr_thresh, , drop = FALSE]
}

# ---- GSVA Hallmark scores, correlated with every embedding dimension ----
# No log transform: ssGSEA ranks genes within each sample, so the scores are
# identical on the raw or log scale.
get_gsva_pathway <- function(rna_mat, embed_mat, max_na_frac = 0.2) {

  common <- intersect(colnames(rna_mat), rownames(embed_mat))    # patients with both
  if (length(common) < 10) return(NULL)
  rna   <- as.matrix(rna_mat[, common, drop = FALSE])
  embed <- embed_mat[common, , drop = FALSE]

  # Patients with no expression at all would inflate every gene's missingness
  rna <- rna[, colMeans(is.na(rna)) < 1, drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(rna) < 10) { message("Only ", ncol(rna), " patients with expression data"); return(NULL) }

  keep_g <- rowMeans(is.na(rna)) <= max_na_frac                  # drop mostly-missing genes
  keep_g[is.na(keep_g)] <- FALSE
  rna <- rna[keep_g, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rna) == 0) { message("No genes below the missingness threshold"); return(NULL) }

  keep_p <- colMeans(is.na(rna)) <= max_na_frac                  # drop mostly-missing patients
  keep_p[is.na(keep_p)] <- FALSE
  if (sum(keep_p) < 10) { message("Only ", sum(keep_p), " patients below the threshold"); return(NULL) }
  rna <- rna[, keep_p, drop = FALSE]

  # Impute scattered NAs with the gene median (one NA corrupts a patient's ranking)
  if (anyNA(rna)) {
    med <- apply(rna, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
    idx <- which(is.na(rna), arr.ind = TRUE)
    rna[idx] <- med[idx[, "row"]]
    rna <- rna[!is.na(rowSums(rna)), , drop = FALSE]
  }

  gene_sd <- apply(rna, 1, sd)                                   # constant genes carry no rank information
  rna <- rna[!is.na(gene_sd) & gene_sd > 0, , drop = FALSE]

  embed <- embed[intersect(rownames(embed), colnames(rna)), , drop = FALSE]  # realign patients
  rna   <- rna[, rownames(embed), drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rna) < 500 || ncol(rna) < 10) {
    message("Too few genes or patients: ", nrow(rna), " genes, ", ncol(rna), " patients"); return(NULL)
  }
  message("GSVA on ", nrow(rna), " genes x ", ncol(rna), " patients")

  hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H") %>% split(.$gs_name)
  hallmark <- lapply(hallmark, function(x) unique(x$gene_symbol))   # pathway -> gene symbols

  gsva_scores <- tryCatch({
    param <- GSVA::ssgseaParam(exprData = rna, geneSets = hallmark)
    GSVA::gsva(param, verbose = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) { message("GSVA failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  if (is.null(gsva_scores)) return(NULL)

  pathway_scores <- t(gsva_scores)                               # patients x pathways
  common2 <- intersect(rownames(embed), rownames(pathway_scores))

  cor_mat <- suppressWarnings(cor(embed[common2, , drop = FALSE],
                                  pathway_scores[common2, , drop = FALSE],
                                  method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))

  out <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Embedding_Feature") %>%
    pivot_longer(-Embedding_Feature, names_to = "Pathway", values_to = "Correlation") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Correlation)) %>%
    mutate(P       = spearman_p(Correlation, length(common2)),
           FDR_cor = p.adjust(P, method = "BH"))                 # BH over all dimension x pathway pairs

  attr(out, "scores") <- pathway_scores                          # reused in Figure 3.2 and 05
  out
}

# ---- Clinical covariates (shared with 05) ----
collapse_stage <- function(x) {                                  # "STAGE IIIC" -> "III"
  x <- toupper(as.character(x))
  s <- ifelse(grepl("STAGE\\s*[IV]+", x, perl = TRUE),
              sub(".*STAGE\\s*([IV]+).*", "\\1", x, perl = TRUE), NA_character_)
  s[!s %in% c("I", "II", "III", "IV")] <- NA_character_
  s
}

collapse_grade <- function(x) {                                  # "G3" -> "G3", "GX" -> NA
  x <- toupper(as.character(x))
  ifelse(grepl("G[1-4]", x), sub(".*(G[1-4]).*", "\\1", x), NA_character_)
}

# Among columns matching the pattern, pick the one with most parseable values
pick_col <- function(df, pattern, parse = identity) {
  hits <- grep(pattern, names(df), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  if (length(hits) == 0) return(NULL)
  n_ok <- vapply(hits, function(h) sum(!is.na(parse(df[[h]]))), integer(1))
  if (max(n_ok) == 0) return(NULL)
  hits[which.max(n_ok)]
}

# Age, Stage and Grade as a data frame. Missing age is median-imputed and
# missing stage/grade become a "Missing" level, so every patient is kept.
clinical_vars <- function(m, min_obs = 0.5) {
  num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  age_col   <- pick_col(m, "years_to_birth|age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis|age_at_diagnosis", num)
  stage_col <- pick_col(m, "pathologic_stage|clinical_stage|tumor_stage", collapse_stage)
  grade_col <- pick_col(m, "histologic_grade|tumor_grade", collapse_grade)

  vars <- list()
  if (!is.null(age_col)) {
    a <- num(m[[age_col]])
    if (mean(!is.na(a)) >= min_obs) { a[is.na(a)] <- median(a, na.rm = TRUE); vars$Age <- a }
  }
  if (!is.null(stage_col)) {
    s <- collapse_stage(m[[stage_col]])
    if (mean(!is.na(s)) >= min_obs && length(unique(na.omit(s))) > 1) {
      s[is.na(s)] <- "Missing"; vars$Stage <- factor(s)
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(grade_col)) {
    g <- collapse_grade(m[[grade_col]])
    if (mean(!is.na(g)) >= min_obs && length(unique(na.omit(g))) > 1) {
      g[is.na(g)] <- "Missing"; vars$Grade <- factor(g)
    }
  }
  if (length(vars) == 0) return(NULL)
  out <- as.data.frame(vars)
  rownames(out) <- rownames(m)
  out
}

# Design matrix of the clinical covariates, for Cox and glmnet
build_clinical <- function(m) {
  v <- clinical_vars(m)
  if (is.null(v)) return(NULL)
  X <- model.matrix(~ ., data = v)[, -1, drop = FALSE]           # dummy-code, drop intercept
  rownames(X) <- rownames(m)
  X
}

# ---- Cross-validation ----

# Random folds, balanced for deaths
strat_folds <- function(event, k) {
  f <- integer(length(event))
  for (lv in unique(event)) {
    idx <- which(event == lv)
    f[idx] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(idx)))
  }
  f
}

# Whole sites go to one fold. Site order is jittered so repeats differ while
# fold sizes stay roughly balanced.
site_folds <- function(site, k) {
  n_site  <- table(site)
  k       <- min(k, length(n_site))
  ord     <- names(n_site)[order(-as.numeric(n_site) * runif(length(n_site), 0.75, 1.25))]
  load    <- numeric(k)                                          # patients assigned per fold
  fold_of <- setNames(integer(length(ord)), ord)
  for (s in ord) {
    j <- which.min(load)
    fold_of[s] <- j
    load[j] <- load[j] + n_site[[s]]
  }
  unname(fold_of[site])
}

# Fit on training rows, return linear predictors (risk scores) for test rows
fit_predict <- function(Xtr, ytr, Xte, type, alpha = 0.5) {
  if (type == "coxph") {                                         # clinical: unpenalised Cox
    keep <- apply(Xtr, 2, sd) > 0                                # dummy levels absent from this fold
    if (!any(keep)) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(Xte)))
    Xtr <- Xtr[, keep, drop = FALSE]; Xte <- Xte[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(coxph(ytr ~ Xtr)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit)) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(Xte)))
    b <- coef(fit); b[is.na(b)] <- 0
    return(drop(Xte %*% b))
  }
  cv <- tryCatch(cv.glmnet(Xtr, ytr, family = "cox", alpha = alpha, nfolds = 5, type.measure = "C"),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(cv))                                               # C undefined in tiny inner folds
    cv <- tryCatch(cv.glmnet(Xtr, ytr, family = "cox", alpha = alpha, nfolds = 5),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(cv)) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(Xte)))
  drop(stats::predict(cv, newx = Xte, s = "lambda.min", type = "link"))
}

# Harrell's C using only pairs within the same test fold, so scores from
# different fold models are never compared. reverse = TRUE: higher score = higher risk.
c_strat <- function(time, event, lp, fold) {
  ok <- !is.na(lp)
  if (sum(event[ok] == 1) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  tt <- time[ok]; ee <- event[ok]; ll <- lp[ok]; ff <- fold[ok]
  concordance(Surv(tt, ee) ~ ll + strata(ff), reverse = TRUE)$concordance
}

# C per model (averaged over repeats) plus patient-bootstrap replicates for CIs.
# All models are scored on the same resamples, so differences are paired.
boot_perf <- function(time, event, lp_by_model, folds, B = 500, seed = 1) {
  R <- ncol(folds)
  cfun <- function(idx) sapply(lp_by_model, function(L)
    mean(sapply(seq_len(R), function(r)
      c_strat(time[idx], event[idx], L[idx, r], folds[idx, r])), na.rm = TRUE))
  est <- cfun(seq_along(time))                                   # all patients
  set.seed(seed)
  bs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(B), function(b)
    cfun(sample.int(length(time), replace = TRUE))))
  list(est = est, boot = bs)
}
```

# Per-dimension analysis

## Survival associations of each dimension

All 768 dimensions are tested in both versions, on the same patients.

```{r survival}
run_cox <- function(E, m, label, cc) {
  r <- get_survival_coefficients(E, m, fdr_thresh = 1)           # keep every dimension
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  r$Correction <- label
  r$Cancer     <- cc
  r
}

surv_all <- bind_rows(lapply(main_cancers, function(cc) {
  cat(cc, "- survival\n")
  pts <- Reduce(intersect, list(rownames(embed_corrected[[cc]]),
                                rownames(embed_raw[[cc]]), rownames(meta[[cc]])))
  bind_rows(
    run_cox(embed_raw[[cc]][pts, , drop = FALSE],       meta[[cc]], "Raw",    cc),
    run_cox(embed_corrected[[cc]][pts, , drop = FALSE], meta[[cc]], "ComBat", cc))
}))

surv_results <- surv_all %>% filter(!is.na(FDR), FDR < fdr_thresh)   # significant dimensions
```

## Figure 3.1 Effect of correction on per-dimension survival associations

**Purpose:** shows whether site correction changed which dimensions predict survival.
**How to read:** each point is one dimension. r close to 1 means correction
kept the direction and size of most survival effects. Dimensions marked "Lost
after correction" should have high site R2 (yellow), meaning their
association was partly driven by site.

```{r fig3_1, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.5}
site_r2_df <- bind_rows(lapply(main_cancers, function(cc) {
  m   <- meta[[cc]]
  pts <- intersect(rownames(embed_corrected[[cc]]), rownames(m))
  pts <- pts[!is.na(m[pts, "TSS.Grouped"])]
  E   <- as.matrix(embed_raw[[cc]][pts, , drop = FALSE])
  data.frame(Cancer = cc, Feature = colnames(E),
             Site_R2 = site_adj_r2(E, m[pts, "TSS.Grouped"]))    # how much each dimension tracks site
}))

dim_df <- surv_all %>%
  select(Cancer, Feature, Correction, LogHR, FDR) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Correction, values_from = c(LogHR, FDR)) %>%
  left_join(site_r2_df, by = c("Cancer", "Feature")) %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
           FDR_Raw < fdr_thresh & FDR_ComBat < fdr_thresh ~ "Significant in both",
           FDR_Raw < fdr_thresh                           ~ "Lost after correction",
           FDR_ComBat < fdr_thresh                        ~ "Gained after correction",
           TRUE                                           ~ "Neither"),
         Cancer = factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers))

r_lab <- dim_df %>%
  group_by(Cancer) %>%
  summarise(r = cor(LogHR_Raw, LogHR_ComBat, use = "complete.obs"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("r = %.2f", r))

ggplot(dim_df, aes(LogHR_Raw, LogHR_ComBat)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = filter(dim_df, Status == "Neither"),
             aes(colour = Site_R2), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = filter(dim_df, Status != "Neither"),
             aes(colour = Site_R2, shape = Status), size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = r_lab, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = -0.15, vjust = 1.4, size = 3.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ Cancer, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Site adj. R²\n(raw)", limits = c(0, NA), oob = scales::squish) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Significant in both" = 16,
                                "Lost after correction" = 4,
                                "Gained after correction" = 17)) +
  labs(title = "Figure 3.1 Effect of site correction on per-dimension survival associations",
       x = "log HR per SD, raw embedding", y = "log HR per SD, corrected embedding",
       shape = paste0("FDR < ", fdr_thresh)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## GSVA pathway scores

Hallmark activity per patient from RNA-seq, correlated with every corrected
embedding dimension. The patient-level scores are reused in Figure 3.2 and 05.

```{r gsva}
gsva_scores_by_cancer <- list()
pathway_list <- list()

for (cc in main_cancers) {
  cat(cc, "- GSVA\n")
  rna <- get_assay(omics[[cc]], "RNASeq2GeneNorm")              # primary-tumour RNA-seq
  if (is.null(rna)) { cat("  no RNA-seq assay found\n"); next }

  res <- get_gsva_pathway(rna, embed_corrected[[cc]])
  if (is.null(res)) next

  gsva_scores_by_cancer[[cc]] <- attr(res, "scores")
  pathway_list[[cc]] <- res %>% mutate(Cancer = cc)
}

pathway_results <- bind_rows(pathway_list)
cat("Pathway correlations for", length(pathway_list), "cancers\n")
```

## Table 3.1 Survival-associated dimensions and correlated pathways

**Purpose:** links the prognostic image dimensions to transcriptional programmes.
**How to read:** each row is a dimension associated with survival after
correction, followed by the Hallmark pathways it correlates with most
strongly. Pathways that recur across rows (for example proliferation or
immune programmes) are the biological themes to name in the text. Rows with no
pathway are prognostic dimensions not explained by Hallmark activity. The full
list is in `Table3_1_full.xlsx`.

```{r table3_1}
# Only correlations passing FDR are attached
sig_paths <- pathway_results %>%
  filter(FDR_cor < 0.05) %>%
  select(Cancer, Feature = Embedding_Feature, Pathway, Correlation, FDR_cor)

dim_pathways <- surv_results %>%
  filter(Correction == "ComBat") %>% select(-Correction) %>%      # corrected embeddings only
  left_join(sig_paths, by = c("Cancer", "Feature")) %>%
  group_by(Cancer, Feature) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Rank = row_number()) %>%                                 # 1 = strongest pathway
  ungroup()

write_xlsx(dim_pathways, file.path(data_dir, "Table3_1_full.xlsx"))

tab3_1 <- dim_pathways %>%
  filter(Rank <= 2) %>%                                           # two strongest pathways per dimension
  mutate(Path_txt = ifelse(is.na(Pathway), NA_character_,
                           sprintf("%s (%.2f)", clean_pw(Pathway), Correlation))) %>%
  select(Cancer, Feature, HR, CI_low, CI_high, P_value, FDR, Rank, Path_txt) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Rank, values_from = Path_txt, names_prefix = "Pathway_")
for (nm in c("Pathway_1", "Pathway_2"))
  if (!nm %in% names(tab3_1)) tab3_1[[nm]] <- NA_character_

tab3_1 %>%
  group_by(Cancer) %>%
  slice_min(FDR, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>%                   # 15 strongest per cancer
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(Cancer, Dimension = sub("slide_feat_", "", Feature),
            `HR per SD (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", HR, CI_low, CI_high),
            P = fmt_p(P_value), FDR = fmt_p(FDR),
            `Pathway 1 (ρ)` = Pathway_1, `Pathway 2 (ρ)` = Pathway_2) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Cancer") %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "-") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 3.1 Survival-associated embedding dimensions and correlated Hallmark pathways",
             subtitle = paste("Corrected embeddings; 15 lowest-FDR dimensions per cancer;",
                              "pathways shown where the correlation passes FDR < 0.05")) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 11, heading.align = "center")
```

# Prognostic value of the whole embedding

## Cross-validated C-index

For each cancer, three Cox models are compared: clinical variables only (age,
stage and grade where available), the raw embedding, and the corrected
embedding (elastic-net Cox on all 768 dimensions). Every risk score comes from
a model that never saw that patient (5-fold cross-validation, repeated 3
times). In the **primary, site-held-out** scheme, all patients from a site are
in the same test fold, so a model cannot benefit from recognising the site.
Random folds are shown in Table S3.4. 95% CIs come from 500 bootstrap
resamples of patients. This chunk takes several minutes per cancer; set
`cv_repeats <- 1` for a first pass.

```{r cindex}
cv_k       <- 5     # folds: every patient is tested once per repeat
cv_repeats <- 3     # repeats with different splits, averaged
en_alpha   <- 0.5   # elastic net: 0 = ridge, 1 = lasso
min_deaths <- 20    # cancers with fewer deaths are skipped
n_boot     <- 500   # bootstrap resamples for the CIs

perf_rows <- list() # one summary row per cancer and fold scheme
oof_risk  <- list() # one out-of-fold risk score per patient (Table 3.3, Figure 3.2)

for (cc in main_cancers) {
  m   <- meta[[cc]]
  pts <- Reduce(intersect, list(rownames(m), rownames(embed_raw[[cc]]),
                                rownames(embed_corrected[[cc]])))   # patients in all three
  m     <- m[pts, , drop = FALSE]
  time  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$time))
  event <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$event))
  ok    <- complete.cases(time, event) & time > 0 & !is.na(m$TSS.Code)
  if (sum(event[ok] == 1) < min_deaths) {
    message(cc, ": ", sum(event[ok] == 1), " deaths, below ", min_deaths, "; skipped"); next
  }
  pts <- pts[ok]; m <- m[ok, , drop = FALSE]; time <- time[ok]; event <- event[ok]
  y    <- Surv(time, event)                                       # Cox outcome
  site <- as.character(m$TSS.Code)                                # for site-held-out folds

  feats <- intersect(colnames(embed_raw[[cc]]), colnames(embed_corrected[[cc]]))
  X_cli <- build_clinical(m)                                      # age/stage/grade, or NULL

  models <- list(
    Raw       = list(X = as.matrix(embed_raw[[cc]][pts, feats]),       type = "glmnet"),
    Corrected = list(X = as.matrix(embed_corrected[[cc]][pts, feats]), type = "glmnet"))
  if (!is.null(X_cli))
    models <- c(list(Clinical = list(X = X_cli, type = "coxph")), models)

  lp_store <- list(); fold_store <- list()

  for (cv in c("Random", "Site-held-out")) {
    fold_store[[cv]] <- matrix(NA_integer_, length(pts), cv_repeats)                        # fold per patient
    lp_store[[cv]]   <- lapply(models, function(x) matrix(NA_real_, length(pts), cv_repeats))  # risk per patient

    for (r in seq_len(cv_repeats)) {
      set.seed(if (cv == "Random") 1000 + r else 2000 + r)        # reproducible splits
      folds <- if (cv == "Random") strat_folds(event, cv_k) else site_folds(site, cv_k)
      fold_store[[cv]][, r] <- folds

      for (fk in sort(unique(folds))) {
        te <- folds == fk; tr <- !te                              # test / train rows
        if (sum(event[tr] == 1) < 10) next                        # too few training deaths
        for (nm in names(models)) {
          X <- models[[nm]]$X
          lp_store[[cv]][[nm]][te, r] <- fit_predict(X[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                                     X[te, , drop = FALSE],
                                                     models[[nm]]$type, alpha = en_alpha)
        }
      }
    }

    # Bootstrap C for every model on the same resampled patients
    b <- boot_perf(time, event, lp_store[[cv]], fold_store[[cv]], B = n_boot, seed = 3000)
    q <- function(x) unname(quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))   # percentile CI

    row <- data.frame(Cancer = cc, CV = cv, n = length(pts), Deaths = sum(event == 1))
    for (nm in c("Clinical", "Raw", "Corrected")) {
      has <- nm %in% names(b$est)
      row[[paste0(nm, "_C")]]  <- if (has) b$est[[nm]] else NA_real_
      row[[paste0(nm, "_lo")]] <- if (has) q(b$boot[, nm])[1] else NA_real_
      row[[paste0(nm, "_hi")]] <- if (has) q(b$boot[, nm])[2] else NA_real_
    }

    # Corrected embedding vs clinical, paired on the same resamples
    row$Diff <- row$Diff_lo <- row$Diff_hi <- NA_real_
    row$Frac <- row$Frac_lo <- row$Frac_hi <- NA_real_
    if ("Clinical" %in% names(b$est)) {
      d <- b$boot[, "Corrected"] - b$boot[, "Clinical"]
      row$Diff <- b$est[["Corrected"]] - b$est[["Clinical"]]
      row$Diff_lo <- q(d)[1]; row$Diff_hi <- q(d)[2]
      if (row$Clinical_lo > 0.5) {                                # only if clinical beats chance
        fr <- (b$boot[, "Corrected"] - 0.5) / (b$boot[, "Clinical"] - 0.5)
        row$Frac <- (b$est[["Corrected"]] - 0.5) / (b$est[["Clinical"]] - 0.5)
        row$Frac_lo <- q(fr)[1]; row$Frac_hi <- q(fr)[2]
      }
    }

    # Corrected minus raw embedding: the direct test of what correction changed
    d_raw <- b$boot[, "Corrected"] - b$boot[, "Raw"]
    row$DiffRaw <- b$est[["Corrected"]] - b$est[["Raw"]]
    row$DiffRaw_lo <- q(d_raw)[1]; row$DiffRaw_hi <- q(d_raw)[2]

    perf_rows[[length(perf_rows) + 1]] <- row
  }

  # One risk score per patient from the primary (site-held-out) scheme:
  # z-scored within each test fold, then averaged over repeats
  zfun <- function(v) if (sum(!is.na(v)) > 1 && sd(v, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)
                        as.numeric(scale(v)) else rep(NA_real_, length(v))   # constant score: no information
  zr <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(cv_repeats), function(r)
    ave(lp_store[["Site-held-out"]][["Corrected"]][, r],
        fold_store[["Site-held-out"]][, r], FUN = zfun)))
  risk <- rowMeans(zr, na.rm = TRUE); risk[is.nan(risk)] <- NA
  oof_risk[[cc]] <- setNames(risk, pts)

  cat(cc, "done; clinical covariates:",
      if (is.null(X_cli)) "none" else paste(colnames(clinical_vars(m)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

cidx_sum <- bind_rows(perf_rows)
```

## Table 3.2 Prognostic value of the slide embedding alone

**Purpose:** asks whether the slide alone predicts survival in patients from
sites the model never saw, and how close it comes to clinical variables.
**How to read:** a bold corrected C (CI excludes 0.5) means the slide carries
prognostic information on its own after site effects are removed. "% of
clinical discrimination" shows how far the slide goes towards clinical
staging (100% = equal). "Corrected minus raw" near 0 means correction cost no
prognostic signal; a positive value means it improved transfer to new sites.

```{r table3_2}
perf_table <- function(df, cv, title) {
  df %>%
    filter(CV == cv) %>%
    mutate(Cancer = factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers)) %>%
    arrange(Cancer) %>%
    transmute(Cancer = as.character(Cancer), Deaths,
              Clin = fmt_ci(Clinical_C, Clinical_lo, Clinical_hi),
              Corr = fmt_ci(Corrected_C, Corrected_lo, Corrected_hi),
              Diff = fmt_ci(Diff, Diff_lo, Diff_hi),
              Frac = ifelse(is.na(Frac) | Corrected_lo <= 0.5, NA_character_,
                            sprintf("%.0f%% (%.0f to %.0f%%)", 100 * Frac, 100 * Frac_lo, 100 * Frac_hi)),
              Raw     = fmt_ci(Raw_C, Raw_lo, Raw_hi),
              DiffRaw = fmt_ci(DiffRaw, DiffRaw_lo, DiffRaw_hi),
              Corrected_lo) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_hide(Corrected_lo) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "C-index (95% CI)", columns = c(Clin, Corr)) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Corrected embedding vs clinical", columns = c(Diff, Frac)) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Effect of site correction", columns = c(Raw, DiffRaw)) %>%
    cols_label(Clin = "Clinical", Corr = "Corrected embedding",
               Diff = "Difference in C", Frac = "% of clinical discrimination",
               Raw = "Raw embedding", DiffRaw = "Corrected minus raw") %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
              locations = cells_body(columns = Corr,
                                     rows = !is.na(Corrected_lo) & Corrected_lo > 0.5)) %>%
    sub_missing(missing_text = "-") %>%
    tab_header(title = title,
               subtitle = paste0(cv, " ", cv_k, "-fold cross-validation, ", cv_repeats,
                                 " repeats; elastic-net Cox (alpha = ", en_alpha, ")")) %>%
    tab_source_note(paste0(
      "Bold: interval excludes 0.5. % of clinical discrimination = (C_embedding - 0.5) / ",
      "(C_clinical - 0.5), shown only where both intervals exclude 0.5. ",
      "Differences are paired (both models scored on the same bootstrap resamples). ",
      "Clinical: age, stage and grade where available. CIs from ", n_boot,
      " bootstrap resamples of patients. Cancers with fewer than ", min_deaths,
      " deaths were not analysed.")) %>%
    tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
}

perf_table(cidx_sum, "Site-held-out",
           "Table 3.2 Prognostic value of the slide embedding alone, compared with clinical variables")
```

## Table 3.3 Added value over clinical variables

**Purpose:** asks whether the slide adds prognostic information beyond age,
stage and grade.
**How to read:** each patient's out-of-fold risk score (from Table 3.2's
site-held-out models, so it is not overfit) is added to a Cox model of the
clinical variables. A likelihood-ratio P < 0.05 means the embedding carries
information that clinical staging does not.

```{r table3_3}
lrt_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(oof_risk), function(cc) {
  r   <- oof_risk[[cc]]
  pts <- names(r)[!is.na(r)]                                      # patients with a risk score
  m   <- meta[[cc]][pts, , drop = FALSE]
  t   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$time))
  e   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$event))
  ok  <- complete.cases(t, e) & t > 0
  Xc  <- build_clinical(m)                                        # same covariates as Table 3.2
  if (is.null(Xc) || sum(e[ok] == 1) < 20) return(NULL)

  y  <- Surv(t[ok], e[ok])
  Xc <- Xc[ok, , drop = FALSE]
  rk <- r[pts][ok]

  f0 <- coxph(y ~ Xc)                                             # clinical only
  f1 <- coxph(y ~ Xc + rk)                                        # clinical + embedding risk
  a  <- anova(f0, f1)                                             # likelihood-ratio test

  data.frame(Cancer = cc, n = sum(ok), Deaths = sum(e[ok] == 1),
             HR = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", exp(coef(f1)["rk"]),
                          exp(confint(f1))["rk", 1], exp(confint(f1))["rk", 2]),
             LRT_P = a[["Pr(>|Chi|)"]][2])
}))

lrt_tab %>%
  mutate(LRT_P = fmt_p(LRT_P)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(HR = "HR per SD of risk score (95% CI)", LRT_P = "Likelihood-ratio P") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 3.3 Added prognostic value of the corrected embedding over clinical variables",
             subtitle = "Out-of-fold risk score (site-held-out CV) added to a Cox model of age, stage and grade") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

## Figure 3.2 Pathways associated with embedding-predicted risk

**Purpose:** describes the biology of patients the slide model calls high-risk.
**How to read:** red pathways are more active in higher-risk patients, blue in
lower-risk patients. A pathway red in several cancers is a shared biological
reading of what the image model captures. This connects Table 3.2 (the slide
predicts outcome) with biology.

```{r fig3_2, fig.width=7, fig.height=10}
risk_path <- bind_rows(lapply(names(oof_risk), function(cc) {
  sc <- gsva_scores_by_cancer[[cc]]                               # patients x Hallmark scores
  if (is.null(sc)) return(NULL)
  r   <- oof_risk[[cc]]
  pts <- intersect(names(r)[!is.na(r)], rownames(sc))            # patients with both
  if (length(pts) < 20) return(NULL)
  bind_rows(lapply(colnames(sc), function(pw) {
    ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(r[pts], sc[pts, pw], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
    data.frame(Cancer = cc, Pathway = pw, rho = unname(ct$estimate),
               P = ct$p.value, n = length(pts))
  })) %>%
    mutate(FDR = p.adjust(P, method = "BH"))                      # within cancer
}))

if (nrow(risk_path) > 0) {
  risk_plot <- risk_path %>%
    mutate(Pathway = clean_pw(Pathway),
           Cancer  = factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers),
           star    = ifelse(FDR < 0.05, "*", ""))
  pw_order <- risk_plot %>% group_by(Pathway) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(rho), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(m) %>% pull(Pathway)
  lim <- max(abs(risk_plot$rho))

  ggplot(risk_plot, aes(Cancer, factor(Pathway, levels = pw_order), fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = star), vjust = 0.75, size = 4) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                         limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "Spearman ρ") +
    labs(title = "Figure 3.2 Hallmark pathways associated with embedding-predicted risk",
         subtitle = paste("Out-of-fold risk from corrected embeddings (site-held-out CV);",
                          "positive ρ = higher in higher-risk patients; * FDR < 0.05"),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
} else {
  cat("No cancers with both a risk score and GSVA scores.\n")
}
```

# Supplementary

## Table S3.1 Survival-associated dimension counts

**Purpose:** shows how much prognostic signal is spread across the 768 dimensions.
**How to read:** compare "Nominal P < 0.05" with "Expected by chance" (5% of
768). Counts well above chance mean real prognostic signal. FDR counts mostly
follow the number of deaths, so they should not be compared between cancers.

```{r tableS3_1}
deaths <- bind_rows(lapply(main_cancers, function(cc) {
  m  <- meta[[cc]][rownames(embed_corrected[[cc]]), , drop = FALSE]
  t  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$time))
  e  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$event))
  ok <- complete.cases(t, e) & t > 0
  data.frame(Cancer = cc, Deaths = sum(e[ok] == 1))
}))

nominal <- surv_all %>%
  group_by(Cancer, Correction) %>%
  summarise(Nominal = sum(P_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            Tested  = sum(!is.na(P_value)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Correction, values_from = c(Nominal, Tested))

surv_results %>%
  dplyr::count(Cancer, Correction, name = "N") %>%
  tidyr::complete(Cancer = main_cancers, Correction = c("Raw", "ComBat"), fill = list(N = 0)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Correction, values_from = N) %>%
  left_join(nominal, by = "Cancer") %>%
  left_join(deaths, by = "Cancer") %>%
  mutate(Expected = round(0.05 * Tested_ComBat),
         Cancer   = factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers)) %>%
  arrange(Cancer) %>%
  select(Cancer, Deaths, Raw, ComBat, Nominal_Raw, Nominal_ComBat, Expected) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_spanner(label = paste0("FDR < ", fdr_thresh), columns = c(Raw, ComBat)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Nominal P < 0.05", columns = c(Nominal_Raw, Nominal_ComBat, Expected)) %>%
  cols_label(Raw = "Raw", ComBat = "Corrected", Nominal_Raw = "Raw",
             Nominal_ComBat = "Corrected", Expected = "Expected by chance") %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "-") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S3.1 Survival-associated embedding dimensions (of 768)",
             subtitle = "Univariable Cox per dimension; counts depend strongly on the number of deaths") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

## Table S3.2 Site signal by change in survival association

**Purpose:** quantifies what Figure 3.1 shows.
**How to read:** if "Lost after correction" dimensions have a higher median
site R2 than "Significant in both", correction specifically removed
associations that were partly driven by site.

```{r tableS3_2}
dim_df %>%
  group_by(Cancer, Status) %>%
  summarise(Dimensions = n(), Median_site_R2 = median(Site_R2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Cancer = as.character(Cancer)) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Cancer") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Median_site_R2, decimals = 3) %>%
  cols_label(Status = "", Median_site_R2 = "Median site adj. R² (raw)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S3.2 Site signal by change in survival association") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```


## Figure S3.1 Cross-cancer consistency of per-dimension effects

**Purpose:** a softer test of replication that uses all 768 dimensions, not
only significant ones.
**How to read:** positive off-diagonal r means dimensions tend to carry the
same prognostic direction in both cancers. r near 0 means each cancer uses the
embedding differently.

```{r figS3_1, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
xc <- surv_all %>%
  select(Cancer, Correction, Feature, LogHR) %>%
  group_by(Correction) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    w  <- .x %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Cancer, values_from = LogHR) %>% select(-Feature)
    cm <- cor(w, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
    setNames(as.data.frame(as.table(cm)), c("Cancer1", "Cancer2", "r"))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Correction = factor(Correction, levels = c("Raw", "ComBat"), labels = c("Raw", "Corrected")),
         Cancer1 = factor(Cancer1, levels = main_cancers),
         Cancer2 = factor(Cancer2, levels = main_cancers))

ggplot(xc, aes(Cancer1, Cancer2, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Correction) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Figure S3.1 Correlation of per-dimension log HR between cancer types",
       subtitle = "Across all 768 dimensions", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Table S3.3 Random versus site-held-out cross-validation

**Purpose:** shows how much naive (random-fold) performance depends on site.
**How to read:** a model whose C drops from random to site-held-out folds was
partly relying on site. A larger drop for the raw than the corrected
embedding shows that site leakage inflates naive performance estimates.

```{r tableS3_4}
cidx_sum %>%
  select(Cancer, CV, matches("^(Clinical|Raw|Corrected)_(C|lo|hi)$")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Cancer, CV), names_to = c("Model", ".value"), names_sep = "_") %>%
  filter(!is.na(C)) %>%
  mutate(txt   = fmt_ci(C, lo, hi),
         Model = factor(Model, levels = c("Clinical", "Raw", "Corrected"),
                        labels = c("Clinical", "Embedding (raw)", "Embedding (corrected)"))) %>%
  select(Cancer, Model, CV, txt) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = CV, values_from = txt) %>%
  arrange(factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers), Model) %>%
  mutate(Model = as.character(Model)) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Cancer") %>%
  cols_label(Model = "") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "C-index (95% CI)", columns = c(Random, `Site-held-out`)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S3.4 Random versus site-held-out cross-validation") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```
